C.2 Concise answers
Each answer identifies the relevant system requirement and evidence. The answers follow the same identity, data, and control paths used by the production system. They distinguish transport success, quality, reproducibility, recovery, and release safety.

Transport success proves only that a request returned; the model can still be wrong, unsafe, stale, ungrounded, or silently degraded. Quality evidence and business outcomes are separate from availability.
The complete serving bundle and upstream lineage include weights, tokenizer, engine image, precision or quantization, prompt configuration, hardware compatibility, retrieval collection, source corpus, and release identity.
DDP replicates the full model and optimizer-related state. If one replica does not fit or global-batch/data requirements are unsuitable, state, tensor, pipeline, context, or expert sharding is needed.
All ranks start together and rendezvous. Partial allocation wastes GPUs while the job cannot progress and can create deadlock-like queue behavior.
RPO bounds acceptable lost work and helps choose the interval; RTO constrains where checkpoints live and how fast they restore. A policy is unproven until a fresh allocation restores it.
TTFT covers queue plus prompt processing before the first token, while ITL describes decode responsiveness. Different optimizations and user perceptions apply to each stage.
It continuously fills freed batch slots and increases utilization under variable lengths. Aggressive admission can increase queueing, memory pressure, or ITL for active requests.
The cache consumes capacity proportional to active context and may be reusable for shared prefixes. Routing considers capacity and locality, while admission prevents overcommit.
Metrics reveal population change, traces localize one causal path, and logs preserve discrete detailed events. Correlation IDs join them.
A judge can be consistently wrong or correct only by unstable majority. Correctness compares with references; consistency measures repeated-run stability.
It makes precedence, overrides, missing branches, contradictions, and ambiguous scope explicit while requiring each node to anchor to prompt text.
Source identities support replay, citations, and failure localization. Full prompts or documents may contain sensitive data, so policy governs sampling, redaction, encryption, access, and retention.
Block exposes a disk-like device, shared file exposes a multi-client hierarchical namespace, and object storage exposes keyed objects through an API. Their update, rename, sharing, and durability behavior differ.
All expected shards and state are validated under a temporary generation, then an atomic completion manifest is published and copied across the required failure domains.
Bandwidth equals IOPS times bytes per operation. Very small operations can yield many IOPS but few transferred bytes.
The new model creates a different vector space and score distribution. A versioned collection receives the new embeddings, evaluation precedes the alias switch, and the previous collection remains available for rollback.
HNSW navigates a memory-heavy proximity graph with strong low-latency recall; IVF-PQ probes clusters and scores compressed codes to reduce memory at the cost of compounded approximation.
Dense, sparse, and reranker raw scores have different scales and directions. Rank fusion or calibrated normalization prevents arbitrary magnitude from deciding the result.
An honest benchmark reports recall, precision, ranking quality, p50/p95/p99 latency, resource and index size, concurrency and filters, build/update/delete freshness, failure and recovery, and end-to-end groundedness.
The orchestrator owns DAG/task/schedule/retry state. The experiment tracker owns comparable parameters, metrics, model/evaluator versions, and research runs; stable IDs link them.
It binds work to immutable inputs and a logical interval, writes attempt-scoped output, validates, and commits one generation so repetition does not duplicate or corrupt effects.
Retries could repeat the side effect or expose partial state. A separate gated promotion task updates the alias after validation and can enforce approval or rollback authority.
Queue, TTFT, ITL, memory, throughput, and HTTP errors remained stable while failures clustered by the new-corpus slice and missing source identities.
Before publication, expected partitions, counts, and hashes are reconciled; the promotion task changes the production alias only after a validation manifest is committed.
